=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.
exchanges.text:
## Executive view

The Seller’s package materially departs from the Buyer’s playbook. The most serious issues are:

1. **General liability protections are materially diluted**: cap, thresholds, basket mechanics and claim period.
2. **The Seller attempts to collapse fundamental/title, fraud and other special claims into the general regime.**
3. **Disclosure and buyer-knowledge provisions are excessively broad.**
4. **Key completion risks remain unresolved**: Bluefen consent, Riverlark debt/security, employee bonuses and Ironquay IP.
5. **Tax and IP have not been agreed merely because the Seller says they are “settled”.**

The Seller’s references to “agreed”, “settled” or “adequate” should not be treated as authority or evidence of Buyer approval.

## Key departures and required push-back

### 1. General warranty cap

**Seller position:** 20% / AUD 4.8 million.

**Buyer position:** 25% / AUD 6 million. The 20% cap is available only with Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying the draft. No such approval exists.

**Push back:** Restore the 25% cap. Do not accept the Seller’s assertion that the lower figure is negotiated or agreed.

### 2. De minimis and basket

**Seller position:**

- AUD 25,000 de minimis; and
- AUD 250,000 aggregate basket;
- only the excess over the basket is recoverable.

**Buyer position:**

- AUD 5,000 de minimis;
- AUD 50,000 aggregate basket;
- once exceeded, the Seller is liable from the first dollar.

**Push back:** Reinstate the Buyer’s thresholds and “first dollar” basket. The Seller’s proposal would exclude many individually material issues and substantially reduce recovery even after the basket is crossed.

### 3. Claim period and general limitation structure

**Seller position:** 18 months, with all limitations applying to all claims unless expressly carved out.

**Buyer position:** 24 months for general claims. The 18-month period requires Amelia Frost’s written approval, which has not been given.

**Push back:** Restore 24 months and expressly preserve separate regimes for fundamental/title, tax, IP, payment and covenant claims. No general limitation should override a specific regime by implication.

### 4. Fundamental and title claims

**Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limit as general warranties.

**Buyer position:** Separate fundamental/title regime with:

- 100% cap;
- at least six years;
- outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.

**Push back:** Reject the proposed administrative simplification. Ownership, authority and capacity are core acquisition protections and must not be reduced to ordinary warranty treatment.

### 5. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct

**Seller position:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all claims.

**Buyer position:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy provisions and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable.

**Push back:** Add express carve-outs. This is a mandatory Buyer position and cannot be waived.

### 6. Disclosure

**Seller position:** Blanket disclosure of the entire data room, public registers, accounts and statutory records.

**Buyer position:** Specific fair disclosure only.

**Push back:** Delete whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search style disclosure. A disclosure should identify the relevant matter with sufficient detail to allow the Buyer to understand its nature, scope and potential impact. The Seller’s own letter confirms that the data room contains unresolved issues, so blanket disclosure would improperly convert diligence material into a warranty defence.

### 7. Buyer knowledge

**Seller position:** No claim for anything known by the Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.

**Buyer position:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier must identify:

- the relevant Seller knowledge persons;
- the information actually known; and
- the reasonable enquiry undertaken.

It must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

**Push back:** Remove “discoverable”, constructive knowledge and adviser-knowledge concepts. They would make the Buyer’s diligence process a broad waiver of claims.

## Completion and diligence-specific issues

### 8. Bluefen consent

Bluefen represents approximately 30% of FY26 revenue. The disclosure expressly states that:

- final written consent has not been provided; and
- conditions in clause 11.3 have not been evidenced as satisfied.

**Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours and consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.

**Buyer position:** Effective consent **and evidence that all conditions are satisfied before Completion**. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for this material customer.

**Push back:** Make Bluefen a completion condition. Require final effective consent, satisfaction or waiver of all conditions, and documentary evidence before Completion. Do not accept consent “on delivery” if its conditions remain outstanding.

### 9. Riverlark facility and security

Approximately AUD 3.2 million remains outstanding and no final discharge is currently provided.

**Buyer position:** Require:

- current payout figure;
- direct repayment from Completion funds;
- effective releases of all security at or before Completion.

A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval.

**Push back:** Reject a generic post-Completion release. The funds flow and completion deliverables must clearly identify repayment and security releases.

### 10. Employee bonuses

DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000, with possible payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. The amounts are not in the funds flow.

**Buyer position:** The AUD 420,000 and all triggered on-costs must be:

- a specific funds-flow line item; or
- funded by the Seller.

**Push back:** Do not allow the funds flow to silently omit these liabilities. Clarify entitlement, triggering conditions, tax and superannuation treatment, and ensure the Buyer does not inherit an undisclosed completion liability.

### 11. Ironquay IP

DD-004 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but there is no independent verification of non-payment or payment.

**Seller position:** Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and considered adequate.

**Buyer position:** Broaden the indemnity to cover the full IP/title risk, including failure to obtain or transfer the Project Materials, related claims and remediation costs, while preserving the SOW3 cure mechanism.

**Push back:** Do not treat AUD 180,000 as verified either as debt or as paid. Require evidence of the current amount and a practical cure: payment, assignment/transfer and confirmation that the Buyer and Company receive the relevant IP rights. The indemnity should not be limited merely to the stated payment amount.

### 12. Export/privacy incident

DD-006 records a download link sent to an unintended external email address and potentially containing approximately 1,240 records. It does not establish access, scope, harm or notification obligations.

**Seller position:** Preliminary and not expected to be material.

**Buyer position:** Preserve logs, investigate, provide continuing updates and do not assume either a confirmed breach or no breach.

**Push back:** Require preservation of all relevant evidence, an appropriate investigation and regular updates through Completion and thereafter as necessary. The agreement should preserve remedies if access, notification obligations, regulatory exposure or loss is later established. Do not accept either the Seller’s minimisation or an invented numeric loss assumption.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals

Three renewals total AUD 330,000. The disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.

**Buyer position:** Assess the renewals; no automatic debt classification or price deduction.

**Push back:** Require details of timing, term, termination rights, accrued amounts, commitment status and business necessity. Do not accept automatic Debt treatment or a price reduction without analysis, but do not accept the Seller’s unsupported ordinary-course characterisation either.

### 14. Office lease and Mossvale

The disclosure identifies:

- an office lease notification obligation; and
- a Mossvale assignment restriction.

It does not establish that either requires consent to the share sale.

**Recommendation:** Verify the operative clauses and obtain confirmations where appropriate. Do not concede that consent is unnecessary merely because the disclosure letter says the provisions do not expressly state it. Conversely, do not impose a condition without confirming the contractual trigger.

## Tax, IP and title

### 15. Tax and IP

The Seller says these positions are settled under the general regime. That is not supported by the Buyer’s authority.

**Push back:** Keep tax and IP terms open and separately negotiated. Do not accept unlimited liability, but equally do not allow them to be silently absorbed into the general cap, basket or time limit.

### 16. Title evidence

DD-012 records the Seller as registered holder of 100% of the shares.

That is a supplied internal diligence source, not independent proof of good title.

**Push back:** Require independent evidence of:

- ownership;
- absence of encumbrances;
- authority and capacity; and
- valid transferability of the shares.

Title claims must remain subject to the separate fundamental/title regime. The register alone should not be treated as conclusive Buyer protection.

## Recommended response priorities

### Must-have positions

1. Restore the 25% / AUD 6 million general cap.
2. Restore AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket.
3. Restore the 24-month general claim period.
4. Preserve separate six-year, 100% title/fundamental protection.
5. Add fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-outs.
6. Delete blanket data-room/public-register disclosure.
7. Delete blanket buyer-knowledge and “discoverable” exclusions.
8. Make Bluefen consent and satisfaction of conditions a pre-Completion requirement.
9. Require Riverlark repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases.
10. Include bonuses and on-costs in the funds flow or require Seller funding.
11. Broaden the Ironquay indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure.
12. Keep tax and IP regimes expressly separate and open.

### Further diligence / drafting requests

- Obtain the current Riverlark payout and release documents.
- Obtain evidence of Bluefen consent and fulfilled conditions.
- Confirm bonus calculations and on-costs.
- Verify Ironquay payment and IP assignment status independently.
- Require the DD-006 investigation protocol, log preservation and update obligations.
- Analyse the Sandbar renewals and lease/Mossvale consent triggers.
- Obtain independent title and encumbrance evidence.

The Disclosure Letter should be revised to provide specific, fair disclosures rather than attempting to deem the entire data room and public record disclosed.
